definitions.explanation: A fine powder or substance that gives color to paint, ink, cosmetics, or other materials. Unlike dyes, pigments are insoluble and remain as particles suspended in a medium.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天然|てんねん}→天然：03560_tennen⟧{顔料|がんりょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{絵|え}の{具|ぐ}→絵の具：16182_enogu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高品質|こうひんしつ}→高品質：18051_kouhinshitsu⟧な{顔料|がんりょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: High-quality pigments are used in this paint.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本画|にほんが}→日本画：18225_nihonga⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鉱物|こうぶつ}→鉱物：04149_koubutsu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{作|つく}られた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧{顔料|がんりょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{伝統的|でんとうてき}→伝統的：04802_dentouteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}われて→使う：00473_tsukau⟧きた。
examples.english: In Japanese painting, pigments made from minerals have traditionally been used.

notes:
The kanji {顔|がん} here means 'color/appearance' (not 'face'), and ⟦{料|りょう}→料：28172_ryou⟧ means 'material.' Pigments are distinguished from dyes (⟦{染料|せんりょう}→染料：16341_senryou⟧) in that pigments are insoluble particles while dyes dissolve into the material they color.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{天然|てんねん}→天然：03560_tennen⟧{顔料|がんりょう} — natural pigment
- ⟦{合成|ごうせい}→合成：12027_gousei⟧{顔料|がんりょう} — synthetic pigment
- {顔料|がんりょう}⟦インク→インク：00120_inku⟧ — pigment ink
- {無機|むき}{顔料|がんりょう} — inorganic pigment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{染料|せんりょう}→染料：16341_senryou⟧ — dye (dissolves into material, unlike pigments)
- ⟦{塗料|とりょう}→塗料：24548_toryou⟧ — paint, coating material (the finished product containing pigments)
- ⟦{色素|しきそ}→色素：19991_shikiso⟧ — coloring matter, pigment (broader term, includes biological pigments like melanin)
